summary:
Measured at a 7-year-old's pace (the vocab audit's reading, listening and thinking times, plus 2.5 s before each tap on the map), the game has about 4.8 hours of first-time content. For a real child that is roughly 6 to 10 hours, or 27 to 44 sessions of 15 minutes (about 5 to 6 weeks of daily play). That is only 2 to 4% of a three-year plan (1,095 sessions, 274 hours).
- **Villa Sol's 21 chapters:** 156.9 game minutes over 13 sessions on 12 calendar days, re-measured on today's code. The run from 2026-10-11 took 180.8 minutes and 18 sessions, because the daily word limit was still on then.
- **The five zones:** 106.7 minutes for all three chapters and the side quests of every zone (68 minutes of that is the 15 zone chapters).
- **Words:** the path the arrow leads a child along meets 156 of the 180 words and 27 of the 50 album animals.
  - 14 animal words are only learned if she taps the animal herself.
  - 4 need a time window (the morning, or sunshine).
  - 6 words and 5 animals only exist at night. Night starts after 18 minutes of play in a session, so a child who plays 15 minutes a day never gets there.
- **After that, nothing new:** there are about 50 to 60 minutes a day of repeatable activities, all over the same 180 words and roughly 30 kinds of activity. So 15 minutes a day is always easy to fill, but nothing new is learned. The friendship hearts and the album fill up within days.

Strengths: the zones fit a good amount into one or two sessions each (about 12 to 29 minutes), the daily activities never run dry, and the word-learning targets still pass.

Biggest weaknesses:
1. There is far too little content for a three-year plan, roughly 14 to 28 times too little.
2. A bug in the arrow: a child who picks "go explore" at the start (and hasn't played the first puppy chapter) is never pointed at a zone's next chapter. The forest's story never started in 3 days.
3. The night-only content can't be reached in 15-minute sessions.
4. Most of the album isn't on the path the arrow follows.

findings.title: First-time content runs out in about 5 to 6 weeks, 2 to 4% of a three-year plan
findings.evidence: Villa Sol's story: 156.9 game minutes, 13 sessions on 12 calendar days. Measured by tools/vocab-audit.js --quick on a copy of the repo (2026-10-21; log in scratchpad/audit2/content-time/villa-default.log; report in repo/docs/VOCAB_AUDIT.md). The 5 zones' chapters plus side quests: 106.7 minutes (zones/zone-playa.json and zones-fix/zone-{bosque,juegos,abuelos}.json, plus zones/zone-montana.json, made by zonetime.js: a bot that only taps what the screen shows, with the child's pace added). Add about 12 minutes of daily warm-ups (Villa was measured with the warm-up off) and 12 to 23 minutes of tapping animals for the album: about 290 to 300 bot minutes, or 4.8 to 5 hours. At 1.25 to 2 times that for a real child: 6 to 10 hours, or 27 to 44 sessions at about 13.5 useful minutes per session. Three years at 15 minutes a day is 1,095 sessions, or 16,425 minutes (274 hours).
findings.impact: From about day 30 to 45 the child meets no new word, chapter, place or animal. The remaining ~1,050 sessions (96 to 98% of the plan) would be the same ~30 activities over the same 180 words.
findings.fix: Size the buildout before writing content. For 25% of every session to be new material over three years, that is about 68 hours of first-time content (about 14 times today's). For 50%, about 137 hours (about 28 times). At today's density (one zone is about 20 to 30 bot minutes, about 2 to 3 child-days, about 21 words), that would be 200 to 500 zone-sized pieces, which can't be hand-written. Plan for content that grows by itself: build the listen-and-do sentence generator out into a longer grammar progression, add one new unit (a place or a season) every 2 to 3 weeks (about 50 over three years), and add goals that last for months.

findings.title: The arrow never points to a zone's next chapter if the child chose "go explore" and hasn't played chapter 1
findings.evidence:
In src/guide.js:158-160, puppyLater() is true when flags.dogSkip is set and Villa Sol's next chapter is c1. In that case chapterLater() returns null in every place, not just in Villa Sol. The only other route is puppyGoal, which comes after playGoal (line 171), and playGoal always has something, so puppyGoal is never reached. Measured with the same bot and setup, comparing dogSkip on and off:
- El bosque: 0 of 3 chapters in 3 days (10.1 minutes; the arrow went to Lupe's pie, the dog's spots, then 'play: Canelo: pay'). With dogSkip cleared: all 3 chapters in 11.8 minutes.
- Abuelos: chapter 1 done, then the zone was used up at 4.9 minutes with no pointer to Abuelo's chapter 2. With dogSkip cleared: all 3 chapters in 10.4 minutes.
- Juegos: the first day ran 13.7 minutes without chapter 1 starting.
- La playa and La montaña only got their stories because the next chapter's person happened to be on screen.

Picking "go explore" (dogSkip) and then not playing c1 is a path the opener offers.
findings.impact: A child who explores first only finds a zone's story by luck. 13 zone chapters and about 60 chapter-taught words may go unfound, and her time goes on repeated side activities and fetch.
findings.fix: Only apply the puppyLater check in Villa Sol (CH.lineHere() === 'villa'), or let chapterLater run when CH.live() is a zone's chapter. Add a test-guide case: explore, then go to El bosque, and the arrow should lead to Elena.

findings.title: Night-only content can't be reached in 15-minute sessions
findings.impact: The 'what you have left to find' silhouettes for these 5 animals can never be filled at 15 minutes a day, and 'met every word' is capped at 174 of 180. The parent sees words on the Learning page that the child can never reach.
findings.fix: Choose one: move the sunset to about 11 to 12 minutes of play; let night come when she sleeps somewhere (a bed in the refuge, or a tent); make every Nth session start at dusk; or add a 'wait for night' choice at a lantern or campfire.

findings.title: About a fifth of zone words and most of the album are off the path the arrow follows
findings.evidence:
Following only the arrow and on-screen cues, the bot met:

| Zone | Words | Album |
| --- | --- | --- |
| La playa | 14/17 | 4/7 |
| El bosque | 15/17 | 6/8 |
| El parque de juegos | 18/23 | 3/8 |
| La casa de los abuelos | 21/28 | 2/8 |
| La montaña | 15/22 | 1/8 |
| All zones | 83/107 | 16/39 |

Of the 24 zone words it never met:
- 14 are animals met only when the child taps the animal and Lola names it: medusa, luciérnaga, abeja, lagartija, lombriz, oveja, burro, pavo, ratón, llama, marmota, zorrillo, carpintero, puma.
- 4 need a time window: the dolphin, hummingbird and rooster only in the first 5 minutes of a session (Z.timeOk 'manana'), the eagle only in sunshine.
- 6 are night-only.

The arrow's tiers (src/guide.js:171) never point at an animal not met yet.
findings.impact: How many days it takes to meet every word depends on curiosity, not on the design. A child who follows the arrow finishes a zone with 5 to 7 silhouettes left. It is also the Pokédex the child loves most.
findings.fix: Add an arrow tier after the zone's story for an unmet animal on this map (Lola: '¿Quién es?'). Let Nico's hide-and-seek use silhouettes of unmet animals. Give the morning and sunshine animals a hint (Lola at the bus stop: '¡Mañana temprano!').

findings.title: Daily activities fill 15 minutes but are fixed, and their goals fill up within days
findings.evidence:
Measured daily activities, days after the first visit (bot minutes before the arrow fell back to fetch):

| Place | Minutes |
| --- | --- |
| La playa | 6.2 and 8.8 |
| El bosque | 5.9 and 7.2 |
| El parque de juegos | 9.0 and 12.1 |
| La casa de los abuelos | 4.1 and 4.5 |
| La montaña | 1.3 to 4.6 (cut short, next finding) |

Villa Sol after its story never ran out in 4 sessions of 15 minutes (villaday/zone-villa.json): 3 favours, Nico's 3 hide-and-seek rounds, the word of the day, Inés's page, the side jobs. In all, about 50 to 60 minutes a day.

Hearts top out fast (H.DAY_CAP 2, H.MAX 5):
- after 3 to 4 days, El bosque has elena, lupe and lola all at 5;
- La playa has marina, tere and lola at 5;
- Juegos has ana and pablo at 5.

The review schedule tops out at 8 days (src/words.js:61, W.BOX_DAYS=[0,0,1,2,4,8]), so 180 solid words keep about 22 due every day indefinitely.
findings.impact: After week 5 or 6 every session is the same favour, hide-and-seek and daily templates over the same words. There is no progression for the remaining 1,000+ sessions, and the review load never shrinks to make room for new material.
findings.fix: Add longer review intervals (16, 32 and 64 days) once a word is solid. Rotate and level up the daily activities: listen-and-do requests with 3 details, phrases combined with listen-and-do, weekly or seasonal events. Give hearts, the album and pages a goal after they are complete (best-friend quests, gold album variants).

findings.title: In La montaña the arrow can disappear when the day's play points back to Villa Sol
findings.evidence: zones/zone-montana.json days 3 to 5: the arrow's goal was null after 4.6, 1.3 and 1.4 minutes. The bot had no cue and was declared used up. A probe in montana_refugio (debug-refuge.js) found G.carry.plan = 'an apple for luna' at granja, which is in Villa Sol. GD.goal drops a goal on another map in another area with no route (src/guide.js, the near() check in GD.goal), so with no other tier the result is null. This is partly caused by the measurement: the bot skipped Tomás's letters because it can't ride the bus.
findings.impact: Once the day's mountain activities are done, a child can be left with no arrow, which breaks the 'never a dead end' promise outside Villa Sol.
findings.fix: Make carry.plan prefer plays in the current area. For a zone, fall back to its own play (the sled, the snowman, fetch with a snowball) before pointing at another area.

findings.title: Pacing claims in the docs are out of date
findings.evidence: The README says the 21 chapters take 'about three weeks of 15-minute sessions'. CURRICULUM.md says 'about 17 sessions'. The committed docs/VOCAB_AUDIT.md shows 180.8 minutes and 18 sessions (2026-10-11, when the daily word limit was still on). Today's code measures 156.9 minutes, 13 sessions, 12 calendar days, with all 73 words met by session 11. The brief says '~55 album animals'; there are 50 (11+7+8+8+8+8). In Villa Sol alone, sessions 1, 3, 5 and 13 end early (4.9, 8.9, 3.4 and 10.0 minutes) because the next chapter waits for morning or evening. Those gaps are filled only if the arrow offers the zones.
findings.impact: Planning the buildout from the docs underestimates how fast the content runs out, by about 30% for Villa Sol.
findings.fix: Re-run tools/vocab-audit.js, then update the README, CURRICULUM.md section 3.3 and the album count. Add a zone content-time measure (zonetime.js, from the scratchpad) to the tools so every new zone's first-time and daily minutes are tracked.

metrics:
## Method and assumptions
- **Pace:** game frames (60/s) plus the vocab audit's child pace: about 1 s + 0.09 s per letter to listen, about 1.5 s + 0.07 s per letter + 0.6 s per card to think, 3 s per word card, 2 s per badge or friend card, 12 s per page puzzle, 2.5 s before each tap on the map. These are game minutes, not wall-clock minutes.
- **Villa Sol:** the vocab audit's bot, which knows where to go (tools/playflow.js). It speaks 35% of the answers and taps a wrong card first 12% of the time. Warm-up, phrases and listen-and-do were off (the harness default).
- **Zones:** zonetime.js (scratchpad), which reuses NaiveBot (it taps only the arrow, the hint hand, bubbles, peeks and sparkles, and wanders otherwise). Warm-up, phrases and listen-and-do were on. A real new game through the opener's "explore", then the bot is placed at the zone's bus stop.
- **Sessions:** 15 minutes each, then save, close and continue on the next date. A zone counts as "used up" when the arrow shows only fetch, nothing, or the bus 3 times in a row.
- **El bosque, juegos and abuelos** were re-run with flags.dogSkip=false because of the arrow bug (finding 2). Tomás's letters to other places were left out, because the bot can't ride the bus.
- **Real child:** 1.25 to 2 times the bot's time (the bot never replays a line, never wanders off to play, and never opens the notebook). One 15-minute day gives about 13.5 useful minutes (about 1 minute of warm-up and about 0.5 minutes to get going).

## Static inventory (from the running game)
- **Chapters:** 36 (Villa Sol 21, of which 5 wait for morning and 1 for evening; 3 in each zone).
- **Words and phrases:** 180 words (Villa Sol 73, playa 17, bosque 17, juegos 23, abuelos 28, montaña 22) and 6 phrases.
  - In the zones, chapters teach 60 of the 107 words; the other 47 come from side quests and animals.
- **Album:** 50 animals (11/7/8/8/8/8). 5 are night-only (pulpo, búho, grillo, tlacuache, lobo), 3 are morning-only (delfín, colibrí, gallo), and the eagle needs sunshine.
- **Notebook:** 26 pages with page puzzles (Villa Sol 11, zones 15).
- **Hide-and-seek:** 43 hiding places (13 in Villa Sol, 6 in each zone), 3 rounds a day in each place.
- **Friends:** 27 with hearts (12 in town, 15 in the zones).
- **Favours:** 36 favour offers from 23 people (at most 3 a day plus 2 listen-and-do).
- **Other:** 5 Villa Sol side jobs, about 25 zone side quests, 15 dog spots, 47 things to pick up, 9 listen-and-do boards, 1 letter a day from Tomás.

## Measured: Villa Sol's story (2026-10-21, current code)
- 156.9 minutes in all, 13 sessions on 12 days.
- Chapter windows add up to 112.6 minutes (median 4.4, range 1.5 to 13.1). The other 44 minutes are greetings, favours, pages and shops between chapters.
- Session lengths: 4.9, 12.7, 8.9, 11.9, 3.4, 15.2, 15.5, 17.0, 15.2, 12.8, 15.2, 14.5, 10.0 minutes.
- All 73 words met by session 11. About 0.47 new words per minute.

## Measured: zones (bot minutes from arrival)

| Zone | 3 chapters done by | First-time content used up by | Daily activities | Words met | Album |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| La playa | 11.2 | 23.1 | 6.2 / 8.8 | 14/17 | 4/7 |
| El bosque* | 11.8 | 22.2 | 5.9 / 7.2 | 15/17 | 6/8 |
| El parque de juegos* | 21.2 | 29.4 | 9.0 / 12.1 | 18/23 | 3/8 |
| La casa de los abuelos* | 10.4 | 12.2 (+2 garden days for the other vegetables) | 4.1 / 4.5 | 21/28 | 2/8 |
| La montaña | 13.6 | ~19.8 | ≥1.3 to 4.6 (cut short) | 15/22 | 1/8 |
| **All zones** | **68.2** | **106.7** | **~32 to 45** | **83/107** | **16/39** |

\* run with dogSkip cleared (finding 2).

## Totals and projection
- **First-time content:** 157 (Villa Sol) + 107 (zones) + about 12 (warm-ups) + 12 to 23 (album taps) = about 290 to 300 bot minutes (4.8 to 5 hours). A real child: 6 to 10 hours, central estimate about 7.4 hours.
- **Days to finish every story and meet every reachable word (174 of 180):**
  - 22 sessions at bot pace;
  - 27 to 44 for a real child (central about 33): about 5 to 6 weeks of daily play, or 6 to 9 weeks at 5 days a week.
  - Villa Sol alone can't take fewer than 12 days.
- **Never at 15 minutes a day:** 6 words, 5 animals and the firefly jar (they need a session of at least 18 minutes).
- **After that, per day:** about 50 to 60 bot minutes of repeatable activities: Villa Sol's at least 15, the zones' about 32 to 45, plus about 1 minute of warm-up. No new words.
  - Review load: about 22 due words a day, steady (the longest interval is 8 days).
  - Hearts: most friends at 5 of 5 after 3 to 4 days in their zone.
- **Three years:** 274 hours (1,095 sessions). Today's first-time content is 1.8 to 3.6% of it.
  - New content for 25% of each session: about 68 hours (about 14 times today).
  - New content for 50% of each session: about 137 hours (about 28 times today).
